task_name: `API.md` and the last leftover of the review both go

rubric.result: The objective promises three things and each is produced by a line of this diff. (a) 'describes the two endpoints as they now answer': /plan-events reads 'whether the plan is being written or is committed' and '`state` is `writing` or `ready`', which is PlanContractProgress.of (READY only when dispatch-check validates and `git status --porcelain -- docs/superpowers/plans` is empty) and the two-member PlanState; /implement-plan's refusals table now lists exactly the ten codes the route can emit — I checked it against implement-plan-route.ts, where ImplementRequestOutcome declares body-not-a-json-object, unknown-field, malformed-agent, malformed-issue, malformed-repo, no-live-planning-session and implementation-phase-uncertain, and ImplementCollapse maps GoNotRecorded/PlanGoNotAnswered/PlanAgentNotResumed to go-not-recorded, plan-go-not-answered and plan-agent-not-resumed. (b) 'names the review nowhere': a case-insensitive sweep of API.md for `review` leaves only the pull-request rungs (`in-review`, `fixing`, `pull_request` 'set only under review'), which the surviving watch still produces; the retired frame, the refusal row and the whole section are gone. (c) 'the one symbol the retirement left with no reader goes with it': PlanProgress.committedAt, PlanContractProgress.committedAt and committedAtArgvFor are deleted, and a repo-wide grep for `committedAt` now hits only the plan, the metrics file and two verdict files — no source, no test, in backend, frontend or plugin. THE MEDIUM SENT BACK IS FIXED AND THE NEW ROW IS TRUE: I counted the sections myself rather than trusting it. `## `POST` headings: line 56 (/start-plan) and line 256 (/implement-plan) = 2. `## `GET` headings: lines 218 (/plan-events), 304 (/implement-progress), 374 (/implement-history), 433 (/active-plans), 490 (/external-tools) = 5. Total 7, and api-server.ts wires exactly that — two `app.post` and five `app.get` (lines 142, 150, 161, 167, 173, 179, 185). The row now reads `| Endpoints | 7 (`POST` 2, `GET` 5) |`, true of both the document and the server.

The brief's line reads '**TDD:** No TDD — the documentation half pins no assertion over its prose, and the code half only deletes a symbol with no caller; the predicates below are what measure both.' No assertion was written down for me to compare and no behaviour goes red here, so the item has no subject.

Both `Final text (backend/API.md)` blocks land verbatim in the file as it stands — block one at API.md:218-227 (heading, 'being written or is committed', the 'this process' paragraph, '**200** with `Content-Type: text/event-stream`. Two frame kinds:'), block two at API.md:238-240. The prose contract of the task is honoured item by item: the `data: {"state":"reviewing"}` line leaves the example block, the paragraph beginning '`reviewing` means changes were asked for on the plan' goes whole, the `plan-under-review` row leaves the refusals table with the four paragraphs that explained it (I counted four in the diff, from '`plan-under-review` answers two different questions' to 'instead of towards a plan nobody can ever implement.'), and the `## `POST /review-plan`` section goes with one `---` separator. On the code half the brief names three symbols and exactly those three leave: `of`, `contractArgvFor`, `pendingArgvFor`, `PLANS`, `CONTRACT_UNMET` and the constructor of PlanContractProgress are untouched, and PlanProgress keeps `of` with its message unchanged. The corrected table row is not governed by any Contract block — it is the repair the previous judgement ordered — and it contradicts none of them.

Row by row over the rows this diff bears on. D-8 ('the plan review retires and the review is the pull request') is served by the last documentation of the retired endpoint leaving. 'What `ReadPlanProgress` becomes | `new ReadPlanProgress({ planProgress })` — no `reviewLog` collaborator' — the diff removes the last port method that use case no longer asks for; read-plan-progress.ts now calls `this.planProgress.of(...)` and nothing else, exactly the row's value. 'What `PlanState` becomes' — untouched, and the surviving assertion `expect(Object.values(PlanState)).toEqual(['writing', 'ready'])` still pins it. 'Which suite covers the surviving watch: `pull-request-review-loop.test.ts`. No task may modify it' — absent from `## Files changed` and from `## Rutas tocadas`. 'The test commands' — the task ran `npm --prefix backend run typecheck` and `npm --prefix backend test`, both exit 0 in the controls log (56 files, 1362 tests). 'Where the two halves of a contract move together' has no subject: API.md is prose and `committedAt` never crossed to the frontend. No row is reopened and none is implemented with a different value.

Exemplars (§3): the one that bears here is `backend/src/application/queries/read-implementation-progress.ts`, 'an application query with a single port collaborator, which is what ReadPlanProgress becomes' — after this deletion PlanProgress carries exactly one method and the query asks it and nothing else. `backend/__tests__/infrastructure/implement-history-route.test.ts`'s idiom (every helper hanging off the test's own double type) is what the edited plan-contract-progress.test.ts keeps: ProgressDouble still owns everything and, per `conventions/testing.md` ('Both failure causes of every adapter are told apart in its tests'), the two surviving cases `a_git_that_does_not_answer_is_a_typed_failure_naming_git_and_not_a_clean_tree` and `a_dispatch_check_that_could_not_run_at_all_is_not_read_as_a_plan_that_does_not_comply_yet` still tell them apart after the four deletions. Rules: AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md — every line added is English; the only Spanish in the diff is the plan quoting the distributed plugin's own `GATES.plan.kickoff` literal, which CLAUDE.md exempts as a value fixed by a contract. `backend/conventions/this-repository.md` — no declared-debt exemption claimed, no TypeScript added, typecheck green. `docs/glossary.md` — nothing renamed. `conventions/simplicity.md` is the document this diff obeys: 'A field, a branch and a public symbol answer to a call that exists... which call breaks without it? Name it. If none does, it goes' — none did, and it went. conventions/defects.md, four rules, one verdict each: (1) CLOSED VOCABULARY — the only classifying value in play is the plan `state`, which stays the closed two-member PlanState; no loose string, no boolean derived from it and no catch-all dispatch is introduced, and what leaves is the documentation of a member that no longer exists. (2) RAW MAP AS THE RETURN VALUE OF LOGIC — no subject: the diff returns nothing new, and the deleted method returned `string | null`, not a map. (3) TWO FIELDS THAT HAVE TO AGREE — this is the rule the previous medium lived under, and the diff now satisfies it: the 'Reaching it' row is a second copy of a fact the `## `` headings already carry, and the two now agree (`7 (POST 2, GET 5)` against 2 POST and 5 GET headings). `conventions/decisions.md` says of an unavoidable copy that it is 'declared and measured with a test that compares the two'; the task's amended Verification pins each half separately (`grep -c '^## `POST' = 2`, `grep -c '^## `GET' = 5`), which removes the slack that let the old single-total predicate pass while the breakdown was wrong — with two numbers there is no composition of sections that satisfies both while contradicting the row as written. I record honestly what it is not: these predicates read the headings, not the row, and they live in a plan's per-task verification rather than in a standing suite, so they bind this commit and not the file forever; a standing guard would be production or test code no sentence of this task asks for. No sentinel is introduced — the `string | null` optional left with `committedAt`. (4) AN ERROR NAMED FOR WHERE IT HAPPENS — no subject: no error is added or renamed, and PlanProgressNotRead survives named for what happened, still raised by `of` on a refusing `git status`. Boundaries: nothing is added at the edge; one `git log -1 --format=%cI` call to an external system leaves with its method. Delivery: no document of either yardstick prescribes a shape of change for deleting a symbol with no reader, and `conventions/decisions.md`'s two-halves rule has no subject here. §3's 'Rules to obey' names no skill, so none was loaded for this item.

Two test files carry `-` lines and the task's own text calls for both; this correction round added no new one. In plan-contract-progress.test.ts the whole `describe('when the plan was last committed')` with its four cases goes, together with the `ProcessOutput` import, the `LOCATED` const and the `ProgressDouble.neverAsked` helper that only those cases used — which is verbatim the task's '**Tests:** removed on purpose: the four `committedAt` cases of `plan-contract-progress.test.ts` ... which pin a method this task deletes'. I read the file as it now stands: its nine surviving cases are intact, none relaxed. In read-plan-progress.test.ts one `-` line removes `await expect(new PlanProgress().committedAt({ located })).rejects.toThrow(/must implement committedAt/)`; the task's own Amendment paragraph asks for exactly that ('The single assertion on `committedAt` is removed from that test; the rest of the file, including its `of` and `ReviewLog` assertions, stays untouched'), and the Verification predicate `test -z "$(grep -rl committedAt backend/src backend/__tests__)"` could not pass while the file named the method. The property the test's name promises is still pinned for every port method that still exists. Nothing that survives stopped asserting.

What the objective promises lives in production files: backend/API.md (the API's contract with the frontend), backend/src/domain/ports/plan-progress.ts and backend/src/infrastructure/plan-contract-progress.ts. The two test files only lose cases — they gain no mock, stub, fixture or hard-coded expected value — and the green suite runs against the port and the adapter as they now stand. No behaviour promised here is produced by scaffolding.

The correction is narrow and I checked it against what the first judgement recorded having read. Inside the files: API.md's hunks touch only the 'Reaching it' row (the repair), the /plan-events section, the /implement-plan refusals and the retired section; the port and the adapter lose only the three named symbols; the two test files lose only the declared cases. The plan hunk, read line by line against the brief (which the program wrote from the plan before this attempt ran, so everything the brief already contains predates this correction): the heading, the objective, the fifth path of `**Files:**`, the Amendment note, the `committedAt` paragraph, the `**TDD:**` and `**Tests:**` lines and the §1 'Known residue, left on purpose' paragraph are all already in the brief's own text, so this round did not write them — the first judgement read and passed them, and the §1 paragraph is the debt declaration `conventions/simplicity.md` asks for, additive and true of what task 7 did. What this round added is exactly two verification lines (`grep -c '^## `POST' = 2`, `grep -c '^## `GET' = 5`) and the clause 'two `POST` and five `GET`, so the "Reaching it" table's breakdown cannot go stale unseen', both serving the finding that was sent back. The amendment disarms nothing: the four original greps survive as context lines in the diff, `**Tests:**` still names what it removes, no route leaves `**Files:**`, and the controls log shows all nine commands green. `### Out of scope` names nothing this diff touched — pull-request-review-loop.test.ts, request-fixes.ts, read-fixes-asked.ts, the go protocol's modules and cmux-plan-agents.ts are all absent.

The diff adds no test: both test files carry `-` lines only, and no `+` line in either creates an `it`, an assertion or a helper. With no new instrument there is nothing to measure for determinism, isolation or real behaviour, so the item has no subject and the test-driven-development skill was not needed. What the pre-existing tests lost is item 6's subject and is measured there.
